title: On Bell's Theorem and Quantum-Mechanically Predicted Perfect Correlations
content: The experimental test of the CHSH inequality confirms the quantum-mechanically predicted perfect correlations between two spatially separated photons. By interpreting the correlations non-locally as the so-called entanglement, Bell's theorem denies the existence of definite polarizations possessed by photons in the absence of measurement. The denial amounts to refuting Einstein's argument for defending his local-realist world view in the Einstein-Bohr debate on the conceptual foundations of quantum mechanics. Einstein's argument is based on his separability principle and his ensemble interpretation of ψ-functions. This paper shows that Bell's theorem is incorrect, and an explanation of the correlations based on Einstein's argument is given. As shown by the explanation based on Einstein's argument, the correlations are deterministic. A formal analysis supporting Einstein's explanation is also presented.
